# Patches

| Id | Reason | Files | Spec | Upstream |
|----|--------|-------|------|----------|
| OS-1 | Serverpod 4.1 compatibility: `OfflineSyncDatabase` implements `Database`, which gained `watch` and `unsafeWatch`. `watch` applies the same CRDT visibility/membership filter as `find` and re-runs when queried tables, `crdt_data_rows` or memberships change. | `lib/src/database/database.dart` | suite 12 §4 | to be upstreamed |
| OS-2 | Web deadlock: `_spaceIdsForQueries` runs membership lookups in the caller's transaction (web SQLite has one connection behind one lock). | `lib/src/database/database.dart` | suite 12 §4 | to be upstreamed |
| OS-3 | Infra: `resolution: workspace` and version `0.0.9` (was `0.0.9+wonky.1`) so the copy is a workspace member instead of a root path override. Serverpod Cloud only uploads workspace packages the server depends on; a path override to a folder outside them breaks the cloud `pub get`. The hosted `serverpod_offline_sync_client`/`_server` pin `0.0.9` exactly. | `pubspec.yaml` | suite 01 §2.3 | not upstreamable |
| OS-4 | Concurrent inserts of the same row id (Sheets' deterministic cell ids: one device types a value, another formats the same cell offline) merged as whole rows: the insert with the newer HLC overwrote every column, so the other device's value was lost. Now an insert of an existing row merges per column: a column the insert leaves null is not authored by it (never overwrites), and a null domain value without field metadata counts as never authored (any non-null value wins it); an older insert is no longer dropped up front. Converges because every replica applies the same per-column rule. | `lib/src/database/merge.dart` (`_applyMergeInsert`, `_applyMergeInsertForExistingRow`, `_shouldMergeFieldMetadataIfNewer`) | Sheets 10 §10 #3, suite 12 §2.1 | to be upstreamed |
| OS-5 | A space whose rows the app purged after eviction (upstream U2 workaround, Sheets weekly purge) came back without the rows this device had authored: the space handshake always sends `Hlc.now(localNode)` so the peer never returns the local node's own changes. Now a space without any local `crdt_data_rows` sends `Hlc.zero(localNode)` and receives everything. A space with rows behaves as before. | `lib/src/sync/engine.dart` (`createSyncSinceHlc`) | suite 12 §2.3 | to be upstreamed (with U2) |
| OS-6 | Deleting rows ran the full foreign-key projection of the table's FK component after every delete statement (~1 ms per row: a 5,000-cell revert took 12 s on the server). Deleting rows of a table nothing references and without unique indexes (Sheets `cell`) cannot change any other row's projection; the tombstones already hide the deleted rows, so the projection is skipped for such tables. Deletes of referenced tables (rows, columns, sheets) still project. | `lib/src/database/recorder.dart` (`insteadOfDelete`), `lib/src/database/merge_utils/foreign_key_projector.dart` (`deleteNeedsProjection`) | Sheets 10 §6 (restores), 12 §2.4 | to be upstreamed |
| OS-7 | Big local writes cost ~0.3–1 ms per row (one tracked call per row: savepoint, clock lock, visibility query, write, ~4 metadata queries; RETURNING of every inserted row; a full FK projection per revived row; on SQLite an attempted-value check that scanned the table's CRDT rows), so a 200k-cell write took ~6 min and a 20k-cell server redo ~45 s. New `OfflineSyncDatabase.bulkWrite` (`BulkRowWrite.insert` / `.updateColumns`, one table, distinct ids): classifies the ids with one raw query, then **new rows** are inserted in three set-based statements fed by one JSON parameter each (domain rows, `crdt_data_rows` with one HLC per row, field records of non-null foreign keys; SQLite `json_each`, PostgreSQL `jsonb_array_elements`) after the existing projection proof; **updates** of columns that cannot affect a projection run as one batched update plus one field-HLC upsert; **revives** of tombstoned rows whose projection provably stays unchanged (new `restoring` mode of the proof: CRDT rows exist, parents visible, no unique indexes, no attempts, only user-tombstoned children reference them) run as one batched domain update and batched row-HLC/visibility, tombstone-generation and field-record writes. Everything else takes the ordinary planned path. Also: the proof's id lists travel as JSON parameters on SQLite, its attempted-value checks join from `crdt_data_attempted_value` (CROSS JOIN fixes SQLite's join order), and metadata inserts skip RETURNING. Records equal the per-row calls' (Sheets `test/sync/bulk_write_test.dart`, server `test/integration/sheets/sync/bulk_writer_test.dart`). | `lib/src/database/bulk_write.dart` (new), `lib/src/database/database.dart` (`bulkWrite`), `lib/src/database/recorder.dart` (`crdtRowsWithTombstones`, `bulkInsertNew`, `canReviveWithoutProjection`, `afterBulkReinsert`, `afterBulkUpdate`, `noReturn` metadata insert), `lib/src/database/merge_utils/recorder_context.dart` (`localProjectionDependenciesAreStable`), `lib/src/database/merge_utils/foreign_key_projector.dart` (`restoring`, `noReturn`) | Sheets 02 §7, 13 §7.5 | to be upstreamed |
| OS-8 | Every sync session synced every space the user is a member of, so once decks are spaces the Sheets replica would download decks and the Slides replica spreadsheets (upstream U1, partial sync). New optional `spaceFilter` (`OfflineSyncSpaceFilter`: `FutureOr<Iterable<UuidValue>> Function(List<UuidValue> spaceIds)`) on `OfflineSyncEngine.sync` and `OfflineSyncDatabase.sync`, authoritative peers only (a follower adopts the announced set; passing one in follower mode is an `ArgumentError`). Each time the session resolves its membership (start and top of every cycle) the filter gets the user's **shared** member spaces and returns the ones to sync; the personal space is always kept. Filtered-out spaces are not announced (so the follower never materializes, projects or downloads them), not handshaked, and inbound changes for them are ignored (`accepts`). A batch callback rather than a per-space predicate so the app classifies new memberships in one query and caches the rest. The server's `SpaceSync` runs the engine with it (the hosted `session.offlineSync.sync` facade has no such parameter): `sheetsSync` keeps spreadsheet spaces, `slidesSync` deck spaces. Tests: Sheets `test/sync/space_filter_test.dart` (SQLite peers: filtered spaces never reach the follower, personal space kept, membership changes re-filtered, follower mode refused), server `test/integration/sheets/sync/space_kinds_test.dart` (PostgreSQL + `sheetsSync.sync`). | `lib/src/sync/space_state.dart` (`OfflineSyncSpaceFilter`, `_filterGrants`), `lib/src/sync/engine.dart` (`sync(spaceFilter:)`, export), `lib/src/database/database.dart` (`sync(spaceFilter:)`) | suite 12 §2.6, Slides 02 §9.2, v2 review Q19 | to be upstreamed (with U1) |
| OS-9 | A synced-schema (registry) change crashed `serverpod start` (Slides S-1, 2026-10-15: `TimeoutException: Failed to acquire pool lock`). `_initializeOnce` re-projected **every** space, one transaction each, synchronously on the first database access; and since `registryChanged` stays true for the process lifetime and the server wraps every session in a new `OfflineSyncDatabase`, every new session's recorder repeated that full rebuild. The registry was persisted before the rebuild, so a crash skipped it silently. Now: (1) **resumable** — `CrdtSchemaRegistry.syncAndGetSchema` persists the pending spaces in the same transaction as the registry change, as `CrdtSchemaColumn` rows `space:<offline_sync_spaces.id>` (seed tables in `dartType`, `*` = all) under a reserved `CrdtSchemaTable` row `#projection_rebuild` (hidden from the returned registry; no module table or migration needed), unions the seeds of a space still pending, and returns every pending space to the context on each initialization; a space's row is deleted in its rebuild transaction. (2) **narrow** — only spaces holding `crdt_data_rows` of a table whose registry entry changed (one `EXISTS` query per changed table, index probe per space) are pending, seeded from the changed tables they hold rows of (the projector loads their FK components); new tables have no rows and add nothing; spaces with rows of a dropped table are rebuilt over every table. (3) **non-blocking** — initialization returns at once; a per-context queue (`OfflineSyncProjectionRebuild.startDelay` 2 s, concurrency 1, one space per transaction, `pause` between spaces) rebuilds in the background under the node lock that writes and merges take, and deletes the marker under it (so another process never projects a space twice); `transactionForUser` (writes and merges) rebuilds a still-pending space first (`ensureSpaceProjected`); reads serve the previous projection until then (identical outside the changed tables; the rebuild is deterministic from the authored state). (4) **never fatal** — failures are logged (`OfflineSyncProjectionRebuild.log`) and retried with a doubling backoff (`retryDelay` 30 s … `maxRetryDelay` 10 min); a failing space does not hold up the others. API: `OfflineSyncDatabase.pendingProjectionRebuilds`, `drainProjectionRebuild()`, `stopProjectionRebuild()` (called by `OfflineSyncDatabaseSession.close`), test hook `OfflineSyncProjectionRebuild.debugBeforeSpace`. Tests: Sheets `test/sync/projection_rebuild_test.dart` (SQLite peers: startup returns with the space persisted, background rebuild of only the affected space, crash mid-rebuild → retry and resume after restart, write and merge into a pending space re-project it first, new tables without rows rebuild nothing), server `test/integration/platform/projection_rebuild_test.dart` (PostgreSQL). | `lib/src/database/projection_rebuild.dart` (new), `lib/src/database/recorder.dart` (`_initializeOnce`, `ensureSpaceProjected`, `_rebuildPendingSpace`, context queue), `lib/src/database/schema.dart` (`projectionRebuildMarker`, `_planProjectionRebuilds`, `_persistProjectionRebuilds`, `pendingProjectionRebuilds`), `lib/src/database/database.dart` (`transactionForUser`, `pendingProjectionRebuilds`, `drainProjectionRebuild`, `stopProjectionRebuild`), `lib/src/database/session.dart` (`close`) | suite 12 §4 (U12) | to be upstreamed |
